Fixed with a flag, a pinned run dir plus exclusion patterns, and a cwd-based line filter.","source":"claude-code:turbo-rig","body_html":"

Problem

The nightly loop's cost grew night over night even on light workdays. Root cause: every headless invocation of claude -p persists its own session transcript under ~/.claude/projects/<encoded cwd>/. Because the loop ran from a fresh $TMPDIR/loopwatch.XXXXXX each night, each run created a new project directory (e.g. -private-var-folders-...-T-loopwatch-a1B2c3) containing the entire input bundle it was fed — a one-word test answer produced a 231 KB transcript. The collector's glob ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl then picked up that transcript the following night, so night N+1 re-ingested night N's input. Cost compounds and stale content gets re-mined indefinitely.

Fix — three layers

  1. Disable persistence at the source. Pass --no-session-persistence. Verified on claude 2.1.283: no project directory is created at all.
  2. Pin the run directory and exclude it explicitly. Always run from a fixed directory, ~/.local/state/loopwatch/run, and exclude its encoded project dir (every non-alphanumeric character becomes -) plus any directory ending in -loopwatch-run, and the older v0.1 loopwatch-XXXXXX mktemp dirs, from collection.
  3. Filter by cwd as a backstop. Drop any transcript line whose cwd field equals the run dir. This catches a moved or renamed project directory that the path-pattern exclusion in layer 2 would miss.

Tradeoff

Layer 2 requires a single fixed run directory, which means runs must be serialized — no concurrent nightly runs. This was already true: the existing mkdir-based lock enforces serialization, so the constraint was free in practice.

Related decision: budget-cap failures

--max-budget-usd is enforced by the CLI itself: a run capped at 0.05 that would have cost 0.066 returns is_error:true with exit 1. Treat a budget hit as a fail-closed outcome: hold watermarks and record a ledger row with skipped_reason=budget_exceeded, rather than letting the same delta re-attempt and burn budget again.

Gotchas

  • On macOS, /var is a symlink to /private/var, so the encoded project-dir name computed from the literal path can differ from the actual one on disk. The suffix-match exclusion (-loopwatch-run) exists specifically to catch this symlink variant.
  • Verify the fix with a regression test asserting the second night's run never contains any line from the first night's transcript.
